title: The walls of Jericho did not fall because Israel was powerful.
paragraphs: The walls of Jericho did not fall because Israel was powerful.
They fell because God was present.
That is what makes the next story terrifying.
Because only days later… Israel walked into a smaller city and got humiliated.
Because one man carried hidden sin back into the camp.
And people who never touched the stolen treasure still died for it.
This is the untold story of why Achan’s secret sin destroyed other people.

many families,
many churches,
many marriages,
many ministries,
many children,
many friendships,
and even many souls…
are still bleeding from hidden sins nobody confessed.
Joshua 6 records one of the greatest victories in Scripture. Jericho collapsed under divine judgment. But before the battle, God gave Israel a terrifying command.
The devoted things belonged to Him alone.
The Hebrew word used is חֵרֶם (ḥerem).
It means “devoted to destruction,” “set apart,” or “consecrated entirely to God.”
Jericho was the firstfruits of conquest.
“Keep yourselves from the devoted things, lest when you have devoted them you take any of the devoted things and make the camp of Israel a thing for destruction and bring trouble upon it.”
The Hebrew phrase for “bring trouble” comes from עָכַר (ʿākar).

It means:
to trouble,
to disturb,
to bring disaster,
to poison the peace of an entire community.
Because later Joshua says to Achan:
Achan’s own name becomes forever attached to trouble.
One hidden compromise contaminated an entire nation.
That is the frightening thing about secret sin.
It rarely looks dangerous at first.
Achan probably walked back into camp looking normal.
“But the people of Israel broke faith in regard to the devoted things…”
But Scripture says Israel broke faith.
Because covenant sin in Scripture is never merely individual.

Western culture teaches:
“What I do privately only affects me.”
Paul later echoes this same truth in Greek when writing to Corinth:

“Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?”
— 1 Corinthians 5:6
The Greek word for leaven is ζύμη (zymē).
Yeast silently spreads through the entire dough.
That is how hidden corruption works.
The people dying at Ai had no idea why God’s favor lifted.
Joshua sent only a few thousand men to attack Ai because the city looked weak.

Thirty-six families lost fathers,
sons,
brothers,
husbands…
because one man wanted forbidden treasure more than holiness.
Read Joshua 7 slowly and you begin to feel the emotional collapse.
“The hearts of the people melted and became as water.”
One hidden sin poisoned national courage.
This is why secret sin is never actually secret.
But you cannot contain the consequences.
Somebody always bleeds from concealed rebellion.
Sometimes generations not even born yet.
And modern Christianity has become dangerously comfortable with buried things under the tent.
But God sees beneath the tent.
“Be sure your sin will find you out.”
Because He loves truth too much to let poison remain hidden forever.
What makes Achan’s story even more heartbreaking is the progression of sin he himself describes.
“I saw… then I coveted… then I took…”
The Hebrew flow reveals descending surrender.
James later mirrors this exact spiritual anatomy in the Greek New Testament:

“Each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death.”
— James 1:14–15
Nobody wakes up one morning planning to destroy everyone around them.
But hell always minimizes consequences before destruction arrives.
And the Babylonian garment he stole is deeply symbolic.
Babylon throughout Scripture represents rebellion against God.
Achan buried Babylon beneath his tent before Babylon buried him beneath judgment.
Some people are trying to worship God while secretly sleeping beside Babylonian idols.
And eventually the contradiction tears everything apart.
Joshua falls before God after the defeat at Ai and asks why this happened.
Because covenant community means spiritual interconnectedness.
This is why parents must fight for holiness.
This is why pastors cannot secretly live double lives.
This is why believers cannot normalize hidden darkness.
this story is not merely about judgment.
It is also about the terrifying mercy of exposure.
Because exposed sin can be forgiven.
Psalm 32 gives the emotional psychology of hidden sin through David’s own failure:
“When I kept silent, my bones wasted away…”
The Hebrew imagery there is horrifying.
Some people reading this are tired not because life is hard…
You were never created to carry secret darkness.
The Gospel is not merely about behavior modification.
It is about bringing dead things into the light.
“But if we walk in the light, as He is in the light… the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.”
God cannot heal what pride refuses to uncover.
And this is where the story points directly to Jesus Christ.
Because Achan’s judgment reveals something terrifying:
Thirty-six funerals happened because God is holy.
But then comes the Gospel miracle.
“Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us.”
The innocent One carried the judgment guilty people earned.
At the cross, hidden sin was not ignored.
That is why grace is so expensive.
And maybe the most dangerous people spiritually are not those openly broken…
Achan stood among God’s people while hiding rebellion beneath his feet.
some people reading this are exhausted from pretending you are spiritually okay.
But Jesus did not die so you could become better at hiding.
He died to make you free.

The enemy whispers:
“Hide or you’ll be destroyed.”

Jesus says:
“Bring it into the light so you can be healed.”
What is buried beneath your tent?
What secret has slowly been poisoning your peace?
What hidden thing is silently affecting people you love?
Do not wait until hidden sin becomes public devastation.
Run to Christ while mercy is still calling.
Someone reading your honesty may realize they are not alone.
One hidden thing beneath the tent can become destruction above the ground.
